name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Liver and Intrahepatic Biliary Tract
aliases: Primary Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Liver
Intrahepatic Biliary Tract Squamous Cell Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Liver

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma morphology in liver or intrahepatic bile duct tissue
Exclusion of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma from other primary sites
Imaging evidence of a primary liver or intrahepatic biliary tract mass with features consistent with malignancy
Elevated serum tumor markers such as CA 19-9 or SCC antigen supportive but not diagnostic
Symptoms consistent with biliary obstruction or liver mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in liver or intrahepatic bile duct tissue with exclusion of metastatic disease and supportive imaging findings.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma from other primary sites, especially lung, head and neck, and skin.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of intrahepatic bile duct involvement
searchTerms: jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable hepatomegaly with firm liver edge
searchTerms: hard liver edge felt on exam
severe weight loss with muscle wasting
itchy skin due to liver problem

occasional.notes: May occur in advanced liver dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Dark urine due to conjugated hyperbilirubinemia

laboratory: Elevated serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Elevated CA 19-9 and squamous cell carcinoma antigen (SCC-Ag)
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing mass lesion in liver or intrahepatic bile ducts
Irregular biliary ductal dilatation proximal to tumor
Absence of extrahepatic primary tumor on PET-CT
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; molecular profiling may show TP53 mutations
Absence of typical hepatocellular carcinoma mutations
other: Histopathology demonstrating keratinization, intercellular bridges, and squamous differentiation
Immunohistochemistry positive for p40 and cytokeratin 5/6

distinguishingFeatures: Hepatocellular carcinoma shows hepatocytic differentiation rather than squamous morphology
AFP elevation common in hepatocellular carcinoma but not in squamous cell carcinoma
Different imaging characteristics with arterial phase hyperenhancement
Presence of primary squamous cell carcinoma outside liver (e.g. lung, head and neck, skin)
Multiple liver lesions typical of metastases
Clinical history of known primary tumor
Adenocarcinoma histology rather than squamous cell carcinoma
More common than primary squamous cell carcinoma of liver

redFlags: Rapid onset of jaundice with hepatomegaly
Unexplained weight loss with abdominal mass
Persistent fever with elevated inflammatory markers and liver mass
references: Primary squamous cell carcinoma of the liver: a case report and review of the literature. World J Gastroenterol. 2014.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the liver: clinicopathologic features and diagnostic challenges. Hum Pathol. 2018.
Orphanet: Squamous cell carcinoma of liver and intrahepatic biliary tract (ORPHA:424975).
